findings.explanation: The add-on assigns all events the sourcetype `cisco:ucs` and puts the class in `source` (for example `cisco:ucs:faultInst`). It has no `cisco:ucs:faults` or `cisco:ucs:audit` sourcetypes, and `cisco:ucs:events` is not an add-on sourcetype either.
findings.quote: Current hardware fault state: sourcetype cisco:ucs:faults (faultInst via the add-on’s configResolveClass poll to UCS Manager). Administrator accountability: sourcetype cisco:ucs:audit, carrying aaaModLR-style changes
findings.suggested_fix: Describe faults as `sourcetype=cisco:ucs source=cisco:ucs:faultInst` and audit as `source=cisco:ucs:aaaModLR`, once a Template includes the aaaModLR class.

findings.explanation: The app id and folder are `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs` (hyphen). Version 4.2.0 is listed as compatible only with Splunk 9.0 to 9.2. 10.x support starts with 4.3.2/4.3.3.
findings.quote: v4.2+ on Splunk Enterprise 9.1+ / 10.x and Splunk Cloud; install on a heavy forwarder for modular inputs and on search heads). The on-disk app id uses an underscore.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the app `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs`, cite 4.3.3 as current, and use the compatibility table from the release notes.

findings.explanation: The add-on has no `ciscoucs://` stanza with `account=` and separate fault/audit toggles. Collection is configured as Managers (splunk_ta_cisco_ucs_servers.conf), Templates of class IDs (splunk_ta_cisco_ucs_templates.conf), and Inputs with `servers =`, `templates =` and default `sourcetype = cisco:ucs`. The advice to override props for `[cisco:ucs:faults]`/`[cisco:ucs:audit]` targets sourcetypes that do not exist.
findings.quote:
[ciscoucs://example_ucsm_domain]
account = svc_ucs_readonly_poll
disabled = 0
index = cisco_ucs
interval = 120
# After you merge vendor defaults into this stanza, you must have:
# (1) A poll that resolves faultInst (or equivalent) into sourcetype cisco:ucs:faults.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace Step 1 with the documented Manager, Template and Input flow, including `faultInst` and `aaaModLR` in Templates. Remove the custom props stanzas.

findings.explanation: The add-on maps faultInst only to ITSI Normalization, and Inventory only for classes such as computeBlade and storageLocalDisk. It has no Change mapping for audit records, and the UC's own dataModelAcceleration text admits the aliases do not exist yet. Listing Change and Inventory overclaims CIM coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: Set cimModels to [] until a site-built Change mapping for aaaModLR exists, or describe Change as a future, custom mapping.

findings.explanation: In UCSM, faults (including the Suppressed severity filter) and audit logs live under Admin > All > Faults, Events, and Audit Log, on the Faults and Audit Logs tabs. There is no User Activities node.
findings.quote: In UCSM, open Admin → Faults and find the same code ... Open Admin → User Activities → Audit Logs
findings.suggested_fix: Use Admin > All > Faults, Events, and Audit Log > Faults (select the Suppressed icon to show suppressed faults) and the Audit Logs tab.

findings.explanation: UCSM `aaaModLR` records usually expose the affected DN as the attribute `affected` (shown as Affected Object in the GUI), not `affectedObject`. If so, every coalesce alternative in the join is wrong and `audit_users` is always null.
findings.quote: for audit, test affectedObject, user, descr
findings.suggested_fix: Pull one aaaModLR event and confirm the attribute name. If it is `affected`, document it as the join key.

findings.explanation: No UCSM privilege named `aaa-monitor-priv` appears in Cisco's privilege lists. UCSM uses roles such as read-only and privileges such as aaa, fault and operations.
findings.quote: the permission label aaa-monitor-priv is the one many\n4.x runbooks use for log-style AAA reads
findings.suggested_fix: Check the UCSM role and privilege reference and name the real read-only role or privilege set, or simply say 'a read-only role'.

findings.explanation: Cisco documents fault suppression tasks as per-object tasks started from the chassis, server, IOM, FEX, service profile or organization (Start Fault Suppression), bound to suppression policies such as default-server-maint. The `pol/fault-suppression-task` path is not documented.
findings.quote: a fault suppression task under pol/fault-suppression-task
findings.suggested_fix: Describe suppression tasks as Cisco documents them and confirm the actual DN pattern of a suppression-task object before quoting it.

findings.explanation: The XML API reference points at the Cisco home path, and the generic Splunk Documentation link adds nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the UCSM XML API programmer's guide and the UCSM System Monitoring Guide fault suppression chapter.

findings.explanation: The sourcetypes, input stanza and GUI paths do not match the products, so the UC was not validated end to end.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Both the main search and the join subsearch filter `sourcetype="cisco:ucs:faults"` and `sourcetype="cisco:ucs:audit"`, which the Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS never assigns; its data is `sourcetype=cisco:ucs` with `source=cisco:ucs:<classId>`. The search returns no rows on a default install.

`business_service` is derived from `prod`/`test`/`lab`/`dr` substrings in `dn`, but an earlier `where` keeps only `^sys/` physical DNs (chassis, blade, rack-unit paths), which never contain org names. So business_service is always `other` and the `critical` bucket can never fire.

Suppressed faults are detected via `lc` containing `suppress`. Cisco shows suppression as a Suppressed severity filter in the Faults view, and faultInst `lc` normally takes values such as raised, flapping, soaking and cleared. Verify which attribute marks a suppressed fault before relying on this branch.

The cimSpl counts every Change and Inventory event in the estate with no UCS source or sourcetype filter, and appends unrelated `head 20` lists. It does not express this detection, and the add-on provides no Change mapping for UCS audit records.

summary: The governance idea (link chronic acked or suppressed faults to the administrator who did it) is sound and the runbook is long, but it rests on `cisco:ucs:faults`/`cisco:ucs:audit` sourcetypes and an inputs.conf stanza that the Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS does not provide. It also claims CIM Change/Inventory mappings that do not exist, gives wrong UCSM GUI paths, and contains a business_service heuristic that can never fire.
